_comment: Durable record of the dialog-commit measurement and the live order that
proved the fix. The October 9 demo order went out at the Toolbox panel's
defaults (0.01 lots, no stop, no target) while every dialog field read back
correct -- because the fields were written with set_edit_text, which sets
the control text without the keystroke messages MT5 commits on.
Measured 2026-10-15 on Alpari MT5 build 6230 (demo account 50000002) with
read-only probes: open the order dialog, write a field, watch MT5's own
committed-state labels, close the dialog. No Buy/Sell control was used.
Finding: set_edit_text leaves the witness labels unmoved indefinitely
(volume witness static through +2s and a TAB out of the field); real
keystrokes (select-all, then type) move them within half a second.
Upstream writes every order field with keystrokes since, and waits on
these witnesses before the click.
The live order below is the proof on a real terminal: requested and
observed volume, stop and target are identical. Entry is intentionally
not compared -- market execution fills at the market price, so the entry
in the signal is informational and the fill price is whatever the market
was at the click.
tests/unit/test_field_commit_evidence.py reads this file, mirroring
test_control_id_evidence.py: the witness identifiers must match upstream's
COMMIT_LABEL_FOR_FIELD, and the fill must show requested == observed.
method: read-only dialog probes (no click) plus one live demo order

behavior.set_edit_text: display only; committed state keeps the defaults indefinitely
behavior.keystrokes: committed; witnesses move within half a second
